pages.name: 1 Overview
pages.title: E-commerce on AWS - serverless core and event-driven backbone (overview)
pages.sub: One account (179330777878), Frankfurt (eu-central-1), three AZs. Layers top to bottom: global edge, API, microservices, orchestration and events, data, VPC. Blue numbers show the main customer journey. Grey arrows show all other connections.

pages.name: 2 Customer (synchronous)
pages.title: Page 2 - Customer flows (synchronous): SPA, sign-in, search, cart, WebSocket, checkout start
pages.sub: The customer browser starts every flow on this page. Grey components are not part of these flows.

scenarios.title: Scenario 1 - The browser loads the SPA
scenarios.who: The customer browser starts this flow. It needs the static files of the single-page application (SPA).

steps.title: DNS lookup
steps.text: The browser asks for shop.tdsynnexlab.link. Route 53 answers with an alias record that points to the CloudFront distribution.

steps.title: HTTPS request
steps.text: The browser sends GET / over HTTPS. AWS WAF checks the request at CloudFront. CloudFront sends a cached copy when it has one.

steps.title: Origin request on a cache miss
steps.text: CloudFront signs the request with origin access control (OAC). Only CloudFront can read the bucket. Return path: S3 → CloudFront → browser.

scenarios.title: Scenario 2 - The customer signs in
scenarios.who: The customer browser starts this flow. It needs tokens for the protected APIs.

steps.title: Sign-in
steps.text: The SPA sends the email and the password to the Cognito user pool with SRP. Cognito asks for MFA when the customer turned it on. Return path: Cognito sends the ID, access and refresh tokens (JWT) to the browser.

scenarios.title: Scenario 3 - The customer searches for products
scenarios.who: The customer browser starts this flow. Search is public and needs no token.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 1 (the SPA runs in the browser).

steps.title: Search request
steps.text: The SPA sends GET /api/products?q=laptop. WAF checks the request. The /api/* cache behavior sends it to the REST API origin.

steps.title: Origin request
steps.text: CloudFront sends the request to the regional REST API. The request validator checks the query parameters.

steps.title: Lambda proxy integration
steps.text: API Gateway invokes the product function. The event contains the full request.

steps.title: Full-text search
steps.text: The function sends a search query to the products index. The index returns the matching SKUs.

steps.title: Current price and stock
steps.text: The function reads price and stock for the SKUs with BatchGetItem. Return path: Lambda → API Gateway → CloudFront → browser.

scenarios.title: Scenario 4 - The customer adds an item to the cart
scenarios.who: The signed-in customer starts this flow.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 2 (the ID token).

steps.title: Cart request
steps.text: The SPA sends POST /api/cart/items. The Authorization header carries the ID token.

steps.title: Token check
steps.text: The Cognito authorizer checks the signature and the expiry of the JWT. The request validator checks the JSON body.

steps.title: Invoke
steps.text: API Gateway invokes the cart function. The event carries the token claims (sub is the customer ID).

steps.title: Cart write
steps.text: The function updates the cart item and sets expiresAt. DynamoDB TTL deletes old carts. Return path: Lambda → API Gateway → CloudFront → browser.

scenarios.title: Scenario 5 - The browser opens the WebSocket
scenarios.who: The browser opens this connection before the checkout. Page 3 uses it to push the checkout result.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 2 (the ID token).

steps.title: DNS lookup
steps.text: The browser asks for ws.shop.tdsynnexlab.link. Route 53 answers with an alias to the custom domain of the WebSocket API.
card: Answer: alias to the regional API domain (eu-central-1)

steps.title: WebSocket upgrade
steps.text: The browser opens wss://ws.shop.tdsynnexlab.link with the token. A Lambda authorizer checks the Cognito token on the $connect route.

steps.title: $connect route
steps.text: API Gateway invokes the ws function with the connection ID.

steps.title: Store the connection
steps.text: The function writes the connection ID with the customer ID and a TTL. Return path: API Gateway sends 101 Switching Protocols. The connection stays open.

scenarios.title: Scenario 6 - The customer starts the checkout
scenarios.who: The signed-in customer starts this flow from the cart page.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 4 (the cart) and Scenario 5 (the open WebSocket).

steps.title: Checkout request
steps.text: The SPA sends POST /api/checkout with the ID token and an Idempotency-Key header.

steps.title: Token check
steps.text: The Cognito authorizer checks the token. The request validator checks the body.

steps.title: Direct integration
steps.text: API Gateway calls StartExecution. The execution name is the Idempotency-Key, so a retry does not start a second saga. Return path: API Gateway sends 202 to the browser. Page 3 continues the saga.

pages.name: 3 Checkout saga
pages.title: Page 3 - Checkout saga (Step Functions Standard) and OrderPlaced fan-out
pages.sub: Payment with a task token callback, compensation on failure, result push over the WebSocket, OrderPlaced on the commerce bus.

scenarios.title: Scenario 1 - The saga reserves stock and asks for payment
scenarios.who: The Step Functions Standard workflow checkout-saga starts this flow.
scenarios.needs: Needs: page 2, Scenario 6 (the execution started).

steps.title: Reserve stock
steps.text: The workflow calls UpdateItem directly with the condition available >= qty. If the condition fails, the saga stops with OutOfStock.

steps.title: Payment task with a task token
steps.text: The workflow invokes the payment function with .waitForTaskToken. Then the workflow waits for the callback. The wait has a 15-minute timeout.

steps.title: Store the task token
steps.text: The function writes the task token under the order ID. AWS delivers the request privately on the AWS backbone through the DynamoDB gateway endpoint.

steps.title: Internet call from the VPC
steps.text: The function ENI sends the HTTPS request. Route table rtb-private-a sends 0.0.0.0/0 to nat-a.

steps.title: SNAT by the NAT gateway
steps.text: The NAT gateway replaces the source with its private IP 10.0.0.10. Route table rtb-public-a sends 0.0.0.0/0 to igw-shop.

steps.title: Create the payment
steps.text: The internet gateway maps 10.0.0.10 to the Elastic IP 203.0.113.11. The provider uses the order ID as idempotency key. Return path: provider → IGW → NAT GW → Lambda. The workflow keeps waiting.

scenarios.title: Scenario 2 - The payment provider sends the webhook
scenarios.who: The payment provider starts this flow when the payment succeeds or fails.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 1 (the payment exists).

steps.title: Webhook
steps.text: The provider sends POST /api/webhooks/payment to shop.tdsynnexlab.link. WAF checks the request.

steps.title: Origin request
steps.text: This route has no Cognito authorizer. The webhook function checks the signature instead.

steps.title: Invoke
steps.text: API Gateway invokes the webhook function with the raw body and the signature header.

steps.title: Find the task token
steps.text: The function checks the signature with the key from Secrets Manager. It reads the task token for the order ID. It ignores an event ID that it processed before.

steps.title: Callback
steps.text: The function calls SendTaskSuccess for a paid order or SendTaskFailure for a failed payment. Return path: Lambda → API Gateway → CloudFront → provider (200).

scenarios.title: Scenario 3 - The saga writes the order and tells the customer
scenarios.who: The workflow continues after SendTaskSuccess.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 2 (the callback).

steps.title: Write the order
steps.text: The workflow invokes the order function with the order data and the payment ID.

steps.title: Pooled connection
steps.text: The function connects to RDS Proxy with IAM authentication. The proxy keeps a pool of database connections.

steps.title: One transaction
steps.text: The proxy sends the statements to the writer in AZ-a. One transaction writes the order and its lines.
card: INSERT INTO orders ...; INSERT INTO order_lines ...

steps.title: Publish OrderPlaced
steps.text: The workflow calls PutEvents directly on the commerce bus. Scenario 5 shows the targets.

steps.title: Push request
steps.text: The workflow invokes the ws function with the order ID and the status CONFIRMED.

steps.title: Find the connection
steps.text: The function reads the connection ID of the customer from the ws-connections table.

steps.title: Post to the connection
steps.text: The function calls the @connections API with the message.

steps.title: Push
steps.text: API Gateway sends the message on the open WebSocket. The SPA shows the order confirmation. Return path: none. The push goes one way.

scenarios.title: Scenario 4 - The saga undoes the reservation
scenarios.who: Compensation: the workflow catches the payment error.
scenarios.needs: Branch of Scenario 1, step 2: SendTaskFailure arrives, or the 15-minute timeout ends the wait.

steps.title: Release the stock
steps.text: The Catch block calls UpdateItem. It adds the reserved quantity back to available.

steps.title: Publish PaymentFailed
steps.text: The workflow publishes PaymentFailed on the commerce bus.

steps.title: Push request
steps.text: The workflow invokes the ws function with the status PAYMENT_FAILED.

steps.title: Post to the connection
steps.text: The function reads the connection ID first, as in Scenario 3, step 6. Then it calls the @connections API.

steps.title: Push
steps.text: The SPA shows that the payment failed. Return path: none. If the Aurora write fails after the payment, the saga also refunds through Lambda payment (not drawn).

scenarios.title: Scenario 5 - EventBridge delivers OrderPlaced
scenarios.who: The commerce bus starts this flow. Three rules match the same event. Steps 1a, 1b and 1c run in parallel.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 3, step 4 (OrderPlaced on the bus).

steps.label: 1a
steps.title: Rule order-placed-notify
steps.text: The rule sends the event to the notification topic. Page 4 shows the email and the SMS.

steps.label: 1b
steps.title: Rule order-placed-fulfil
steps.text: The rule sends the event to the order buffer queue. The queue protects the 3PL link from peaks. Page 4 shows the fulfillment.

steps.label: 1c
steps.title: Rule commerce-log
steps.text: The rule invokes the producer function in the VPC.

steps.title: Event log
steps.text: The function writes the event to the Kafka topic commerce-events with IAM authentication.
card: key o-1001, value = the event JSON

steps.title: Failed delivery
steps.text: If a target still fails after all retries, EventBridge sends the event to the DLQ of that rule. Return path: none. The bus archive keeps every event for replay.
card: SQS message in the rule DLQ

pages.name: 4 Fulfillment + notifications
pages.title: Page 4 - Fulfillment over Amazon MQ and customer notifications
pages.sub: FulfillOrder goes to the 3PL over the VPN. ShipmentDispatched comes back through EventBridge Pipes. SNS fans out to email, SMS and back office.

scenarios.title: Scenario 1 - The fulfillment command goes to the 3PL
scenarios.who: The order buffer queue starts this flow.
scenarios.needs: Needs: page 3, Scenario 5, step 1b (OrderPlaced in the buffer).

steps.title: Poll
steps.text: The event source mapping polls the queue and invokes the function with a batch. The function reports only the failed items.

steps.title: Publish FulfillOrder
steps.text: The function publishes a persistent FulfillOrder message to the fulfillment exchange over AMQPS. The broker confirms each message.

steps.title: To the VPN
steps.text: The broker sends the message on the AMQPS connection that the WMS opened. Route table rtb-private-a sends 172.16.0.0/16 to vgw-shop.

steps.title: Delivery
steps.text: The Site-to-Site VPN carries the message to the customer gateway of the 3PL. The WMS reads the message and sends an ack. Return path: the ack goes back the same way to the broker.
card: IPsec tunnel to the 3PL customer gateway

scenarios.title: Scenario 2 - The 3PL reports the shipment
scenarios.who: The 3PL WMS starts this flow when a parcel leaves the warehouse.

steps.title: Publish ShipmentDispatched
steps.text: The WMS publishes the message to the shipments exchange over the VPN.

steps.title: Into the VPC
steps.text: The virtual private gateway delivers the packets to the broker. The broker stores the message in the queue shipments.events.

steps.title: Poll
steps.text: The pipe reads batches from the queue. Its filter passes only ShipmentDispatched messages. An MQ source runs 5 pollers. A quota increase gives more.
card: Pipe source: Amazon MQ queue shipments.events

steps.title: Publish to the bus
steps.text: The pipe sends the event to the commerce bus with detail-type ShipmentDispatched.

steps.title: Rule shipment-notify
steps.text: The rule sends the event to the notification topic. Scenarios 3 and 4 continue. Return path: none. The pipe acknowledges the messages after the delivery.

scenarios.title: Scenario 3 - The customer gets an email
scenarios.who: The notification topic starts this flow.
scenarios.needs: Needs: page 3, Scenario 5, step 1a, or Scenario 2, step 5.

steps.title: Fan-out
steps.text: The topic sends a copy to the email queue with raw message delivery.
card: SQS message, body = the event JSON (raw)

steps.title: Poll
steps.text: The event source mapping invokes the email function with a batch.

steps.title: Send the email
steps.text: The function selects the template from the event type. It calls SendEmail with the configuration set.

steps.title: Delivery
steps.text: SES delivers the email to the mailbox of the customer. Return path: the configuration set sends bounce and complaint events to the EventBridge default bus.
card: SMTP to the mail server of the customer

scenarios.title: Scenario 4 - The customer gets an SMS
scenarios.who: The notification topic starts this flow.
scenarios.needs: Needs: the same event as Scenario 3.

steps.title: Fan-out
steps.text: The topic sends a copy to the SMS queue. A filter policy passes only customers who accept SMS.

steps.title: Poll
steps.text: The event source mapping invokes the SMS function.

steps.title: Send the SMS
steps.text: The function calls SendTextMessage of AWS End User Messaging SMS.

steps.title: Delivery
steps.text: The SMS goes to the phone of the customer. Return path: none.

scenarios.title: Scenario 5 - The back office gets a copy
scenarios.who: The notification topic starts this flow.
scenarios.needs: Needs: the same event as Scenario 3.

steps.title: Fan-out
steps.text: The topic sends a copy to the back-office queue. The back-office application reads it. That application is outside this design. Return path: none.

pages.name: 5 Admin + analytics
pages.title: Page 5 - Catalog administration, image processing and clickstream analytics
pages.sub: Catalog writes reach OpenSearch through the DynamoDB zero-ETL integration. Images resize on upload. Clickstream goes through MSK to the data lake and the counters.

scenarios.title: Scenario 1 - The admin saves a product
scenarios.who: A back-office admin starts this flow from the admin pages of the SPA.
scenarios.needs: Needs: the admin signed in with MFA (as on page 2, Scenario 2).

steps.title: Admin request
steps.text: The admin pages send PUT /api/admin/products/SKU#123 with the ID token.

steps.title: Token and group check
steps.text: The authorizer accepts only tokens with the admins group claim. The request validator checks the product body.

steps.title: Invoke
steps.text: API Gateway invokes the product function on the admin route.

steps.title: Write the product
steps.text: The function writes the product item. DynamoDB Streams records the change. Return path: Lambda → API Gateway → CloudFront → admin.
card: stream record with the new image

scenarios.title: Scenario 2 - Zero-ETL copies the change to OpenSearch
scenarios.who: The DynamoDB stream starts this flow.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 1 (the stream record).

steps.title: Read the stream
steps.text: The OpenSearch Ingestion pipeline of the zero-ETL integration reads the DynamoDB stream. The first full copy came from a point-in-time recovery (PITR) export.

steps.title: Index the document
steps.text: The pipeline writes the document to the products index. Search shows the change after a short delay. Return path: none.

scenarios.title: Scenario 3 - The admin gets a presigned upload URL
scenarios.who: A back-office admin starts this flow before an image upload.
scenarios.needs: Needs: the admin signed in with MFA.

steps.title: Request
steps.text: The admin pages send POST /api/admin/images/upload-url with the ID token.

steps.title: Token and group check
steps.text: The authorizer accepts only tokens with the admins group claim.

steps.title: Sign the URL
steps.text: The function signs a PUT URL for the uploads bucket. It does not call S3. Return path: the URL goes back to the admin. The URL expires after a short time (for example 5 minutes).

scenarios.title: Scenario 4 - The admin browser uploads the image
scenarios.who: The admin browser starts this flow.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 3 (the presigned URL).

steps.title: Upload
steps.text: The browser sends the file with HTTPS PUT to the presigned URL. The upload does not use CloudFront or API Gateway. Return path: S3 sends 200 to the browser.

scenarios.title: Scenario 5 - S3 starts the image resize
scenarios.who: The uploads bucket starts this flow.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 4 (the new object).

steps.title: Object Created event
steps.text: The bucket sends an Object Created event to the EventBridge default bus. S3 sends its events only to the default bus.

steps.title: Rule image-uploaded
steps.text: The rule matches the uploads bucket and invokes the resize function. A DLQ keeps failed deliveries.

steps.title: Read the original
steps.text: The function reads the original image with GetObject.

steps.title: Write the sizes
steps.text: The function writes three sizes to the web bucket. CloudFront serves them under /images/*. Return path: none. The separate bucket prevents a resize loop.

scenarios.title: Scenario 6 - The browser sends clickstream events
scenarios.who: The customer browser starts this flow while the customer uses the shop.
scenarios.needs: Needs: page 2, Scenario 1 (the SPA runs).

steps.title: Event batch
steps.text: The SPA sends POST /api/events with a batch of page views and clicks.

steps.title: Origin request
steps.text: CloudFront sends the batch to the REST API. Throttling on the /events route limits the request rate.

steps.title: Invoke
steps.text: API Gateway invokes the producer function. The function runs in the VPC because the browser cannot speak Kafka.
card: Lambda event, body = the event batch

steps.title: Produce
steps.text: The function writes the events to the topic clickstream. The key is the session ID. Return path: Lambda → API Gateway → CloudFront → browser (202).

scenarios.title: Scenario 7 - A consumer writes the data lake
scenarios.who: MSK Serverless starts this flow through an event source mapping.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 6 (or page 3, Scenario 5, step 2 for commerce events).

steps.title: Poll
steps.text: The event source mapping in provisioned mode reads batches. Its consumer group is archive.

steps.title: Write a batch file
steps.text: The function writes one file for each batch. The object key has date and hour partitions. The marketing team queries this data. Return path: none.

scenarios.title: Scenario 8 - A consumer counts popular products
scenarios.who: MSK Serverless starts this flow through a second event source mapping.
scenarios.needs: Needs: Scenario 6.

steps.title: Poll
steps.text: A second event source mapping reads the same topic. Its consumer group is counters.

steps.title: Update the counters
steps.text: The function adds the view counts for each SKU with an atomic ADD. The product function reads these counters. Return path: none.
